review_notes: I read the whole target file (two theorems). I grepped the repo for repeated machinery. The perfect-group, small-index, permutation-representation argument is proved from scratch at least four times: here, in TriageSL4Gen, in NQTermPerfectSmallFamily and in CaseHU33 (the last is the index ≤ 3 variant). GapsPerfect.lean also holds a reusable lemma, `perm_hom_eq_one_of_perfect`, which covers the first half of this argument. Other things I looked at: inside the second theorem, the local `hmm` lemma (conjugation by a product) is a short calculation, so I did not report it. Repeated `Equiv.Perm.isSolvable` one-liners across the repo are too small to report. I did not check whether the target's transitive imports already include any of the duplicate files. findings.problem: The target reproves, from scratch, the standard fact that a finite perfect group has no proper subgroup of index ≤ 4. The proof goes through the coset action `MulAction.toPermHom`, a solvable `Perm` of a set of at most 4 points, a trivial image, and finally `St.inv_mem` applied to the stabiliser of the coset of 1. The same argument is already written out in separate files: `eq_top_of_index_le_four` in RouteD/TriageSL4Gen.lean (same statement, `[Group.IsPerfect L]` instead of `commutator W = ⊤`), `eq_top_of_index_le_four` in H13/NQTermPerfectSmallFamily.lean (with an `index ≠ 0` hypothesis), and `CaseH.eq_top_of_index_le_three` in Timmesfeld/ARS/CaseHU33.lean. The last three all end with the same `h2 : k • ((1 : K) : K ⧸ H) = ...` / `MulAction.Quotient.smul_mk, smul_eq_mul, mul_one, QuotientGroup.eq` rewrite chain. The first half (perfect group → trivial hom to a solvable group) is also available as `perm_hom_eq_one_of_perfect` in RouteD/GapsPerfect.lean, and `perfect_smul_eq_of_card_le_four` there gives `l • a = a` directly. The target then uses the result as `eq_top_of_perfect_of_index_le_four hDperf St (by omega)`, so any fix to this argument has to be made in several places.
findings.proposed_change: Keep one general lemma in a low-level shared file, e.g. `theorem eq_top_of_index_le_four {L : Type*} [Group L] [Finite L] [Group.IsPerfect L] {H : Subgroup L} (hH : H.index ≤ 4) : H = ⊤`. Proof sketch: `perfect_smul_eq_of_card_le_four` (or `perm_hom_eq_one_of_perfect`) applied to `L ⧸ H`, whose `Nat.card` is `H.index`, gives `g • ((1 : L) : L ⧸ H) = (1 : L ⧸ H)` for all `g`. Then `MulAction.Quotient.smul_mk` and `QuotientGroup.eq` give `g⁻¹ ∈ H`. Alternatively, move `eq_top_of_index_le_four` from TriageSL4Gen.lean, and its `[Finite L]` hypothesis is already in the target's setting, to a shared file, since GapsPerfect.lean imports only Mathlib. Then delete the target's copy and the NQTerm copy. Rewrite the CaseHU33 `index ≤ 3` version as `eq_top_of_index_le_four (hH.trans (by norm_num))`, which removes its `isSolvable_perm_of_card_le_three` dependence from this use. In the target, `haveI : Group.IsPerfect W := ⟨hW⟩` (the class has a single field `commutator_eq_top`) lets the first theorem become the shared lemma, or it can be dropped. The use at `eq_top_of_perfect_of_index_le_four hDperf St (by omega)` becomes `haveI : Group.IsPerfect D := ⟨hDperf⟩; eq_top_of_index_le_four (H := St) (by omega)`. The `Finite W` and `Finite D` hypotheses are already available there from `[Finite G]`.
findings.benefit: There is one maintained proof of a frequently used fact instead of at least four slightly different ones, which use different solvability devices (`eq_bot_of_commutator_eq_self_of_le`, derivedSeries, `Subsingleton φ.range`). Readers can recognise the fact by name instead of re-checking a 20-line coset-action argument. The target file shrinks by about 20 lines, and its imports no longer need to support this local reproof.
